summary: Colorado places the roof rat on its Domestic Animal List: 2 CCR 406-11 §1103(A) lists 'domesticated races of rats (Rattus norvegicus and Rattus)' — a genus-level entry covering Rattus rattus — which exempts captive-bred rats from Parks & Wildlife licensing entirely, and the genus isn't on the prohibited-species list. So keeping a captive-bred roof rat is legal with no CPW license. Breeding/selling is legal as a hobby; at commercial scale (above ~200 rats/mice/gerbils/hamsters transferred per year) a Colorado Dept of Agriculture PACFA license applies. Importing needs a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection; never release one.

keep.why: 2 CCR 406-11 §1103(A) places 'domesticated races of rats (Rattus norvegicus and Rattus)' on the Domestic Animal List, exempting them from all CPW wildlife licensing; CPW states it doesn't manage domestic rats/mice, and Rattus is not on the prohibited-species list (2 CCR 406-0-008). No license to keep a captive-bred roof rat. (The exemption is for 'domesticated races'/captive-bred, not wild-caught.)

breed.why: No CPW wildlife breeding license is needed for a domestic-list animal. Colorado's PACFA (C.R.S. §35-80) covers rats, but a small-animal hobby breeder is EXEMPT below the Commissioner's threshold (currently ~200 rats/mice/gerbils/hamsters combined transferred per year); above it, a PACFA small-animal breeder license applies.

sell_give.why: Transfers of a domestic-list animal need no CPW permit. PACFA governs commercial transfer of pet animals (rats included): transferring/selling/adopting-out MORE than ~200 rats (combined with mice/gerbils/hamsters) per year requires a Colorado Dept of Agriculture PACFA license; below that, free giving/adoption and small sales are legal without one.

transport.why: Intrastate movement of a domestic-list animal needs no CPW transport permit or in-state health certificate. Interstate IMPORT requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (within 30 days) for small/pocket pets from the Colorado Dept of Agriculture. The no-release rule (2 CCR 406-11) bars ever releasing one into the wild.
transport.governing_law: 8 CCR 1201-19 (CDA import); CDA 'Bringing Small Animals into Colorado'; 2 CCR 406-11 (no-release).

restrictions.summary: Transferring more than ~200 rats/mice/gerbils/hamsters (combined) per year makes you a PACFA-licensed small-animal breeder/dealer (Colorado Dept of Agriculture; ~$425 + inspection). Below the threshold, hobby breeding and free adoption need no license.
steps: Stay under the PACFA small-animal threshold, or obtain a PACFA license

restrictions.summary: Importing a pet rat into Colorado requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (within 30 days). No CVI for in-state movement. Never release a roof rat.
restrictions.where_to_file: Colorado Dept of Agriculture, Animal Health Division
